name: Vibra - the montage we always build
note: The real rig, position by position, as described by the owner on 2026-08-25
from a video of the get-in. This is a written plot, not a generated one:
`qlctool stage --plot` writes it into the workspace's <Monitor> verbatim.
The stage is in metres and the positions in millimetres, which is what QLC+
stores. A fixture position is its NEAR CORNER, not its centre, so every x
and z here is the line it sits on minus half the fixture's own size. That is
what makes a row read as evenly spaced rather than evenly left-aligned, and
what puts a beam in the middle of its flightcase instead of over the edge.
z grows TOWARDS THE AUDIENCE. QLC+'s 3D camera starts at +Z looking at -Z
(MainView3D::resetCameraPosition), so the far side of the stage is small z
and the front edge is large z. Getting this backwards mirrors the whole rig.
x_rot is degrees about the horizontal axis, and QLC+ turns the fixture by
MINUS the stored angle (MonitorProperties::fixtureRotationMatrix). WHICH WAY
THE LIGHT THEN GOES DEPENDS ON THE FIXTURE TYPE. A fixture with a mesh - PAR,
moving head - emits down (0,-1,0), so POSITIVE leans it out over the audience
and negative back over the stage: the truss PARs are at 50 and the two
downstage grids at -35. A fixture QLC+ draws itself - LED Bar (Pixels), LED
Bar (Beams), Strobe - emits from its TOP face (PixelBar3DItem.qml puts each
head's plane at +phySize.y/2), so the sign is the other way round: the pixel
panels and the LED bars face the room at -90. Both halves of this were found
in the 3D view on 2026-08-25, one flip at a time.
A MOVING HEAD is mounted, not aimed - 0 hanging, 180 standing on the
floor - because pan and tilt are what point it, and the show drives those.
`qlctool stage --plot` prints where every beam meets the floor; use it.
props are scenery, not fixtures - given as a centre and a size in mm.
Eight patched fixtures are not built into this montage - they come from
bigger setups. They keep a parking spot and are marked hidden so the 2D and
3D views only show what is actually rigged.
